chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, who said:
Whoever wants to gain flesh (weight), let him enter the bathhouse one day and be absent from it one day; and whoever wants to slim down and is of much flesh, let him enter the bathhouse every day.
ai.seo_question: How should one use the bathhouse to gain or lose weight according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*’s chapter on the bathhouse, this hadith illustrates the early Islamic emphasis on *al-tibb al-nabawi* (Prophetic medicine) by linking hygiene routines to constitutional health management. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing the bathhouse not merely as a place of cleanliness but as a therapeutic tool for regulating bodily humors and physical strength. This practical guidance underscores the holistic approach to well-being where ritual purity and physical health are mutually reinforcing.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(He<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘

The one who wants to carry flesh (to gain weight) so let him enter the bathhouse one day, and be absent from it one day, and the one who intends slimming and he was of a lot of flesh, so let him enter the bathhouse every day’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from a man of banu Hashim who has said the following: “I once entered in dark house where a group of banu Hashim were and I offered them greeting of peace with the phrase of offering greeting. A certain one among them said, ‘Offer greeting of peace to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, he is in the center.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I offered him (the Imam) greeting of peace and sat in front of him and said, “Since a long time I loved to visit you to ask about certain things.’” He (the Imam) said, ‘Ask whatever you like.’

I then asked, ‘What do you say about using a bathhouse?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not enter a bathhouse without a loincloth, keep your eyes cast down, do not wash with used water because fornicators take a bath with it as well as those bom out of wedlock, and enemies of Ah/ al-Bayt, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, who are the worst of them. 5 ”
